clue.text: Where to expect the green shoots of growth domestically?

definitions.text: Where to expect the green shoots of growth domestically?

blocks.note: surface reading: the economic phrase for early signs of recovery in a national economy

blocks.clueFragment: Where to expect the green shoots of growth domestically?
blocks.note: setter's reading: literal green shoots, sprouting in a plot at home where produce is grown

explanation.surface: An economist asks where signs of recovery in the home economy might appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green shoots' and 'domestically' borrow the language of economic recovery, but read literally they mean growing plants at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot by a house where vegetables are grown is where literal green shoots come up at home.

clue.text: Here, north of the border trafficking involved a US narc

indicators.note: trafficking means dealing and moving goods around, so the letters that follow are moved around too

blocks.note: the fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cross-border drug-trafficking case up north has drawn in an American narcotics agent.
explanation.walkthrough: A narc is a US narcotics officer. The island lies just north of the US-Canada border, off British Columbia, a known smuggling route.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canadian island sits just over the border from Washington State, so it is a place north of the frontier.

clue.text: Pull a face cutting head off fat fish

indicators.note: cutting the head off a word removes its first letter

blocks.note: to gurn is to pull a grotesque face

explanation.surface: Someone grimaces while trimming the fatty head from a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Gurning, pulling faces, is a British folk contest; LARD loses its L.
explanation.definitionFit: The gurnard is a bottom-dwelling sea fish with a large bony head.

clue.text: Merchant called Garfunkel turned up to welcome son

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning something up flips it so it reads from bottom to top
welcoming a guest means taking them inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: called as in given a name
Art Garfunkel, of Simon and Garfunkel

explanation.surface: A trader named Garfunkel arrives to greet his son.
explanation.walkthrough: NAMED ART read upwards gives TRADEMAN, and the S is welcomed into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman is one who buys and sells goods, a shopkeeper or dealer, which is what a merchant is.

clue.text: Section of band runs into singer

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

blocks.note: a bass is a low-voiced singer
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Part of a band dashes over to a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The brass are the trumpets, trombones and horns, one section of an orchestra or band.

clue.text: Of efficient design, hence without microphone

explanation.surface: A sleek design that therefore manages without a microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergonomic describes things shaped for comfortable, efficient use by people.

clue.text: Range-bound gold market

indicators.note: something bound is wrapped round and held in, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: an Aga is a British brand of range cooker

explanation.surface: A commodities report: gold trading stays within a narrow range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range-bound' is market jargon for prices stuck in a band; here a kitchen range is wrapped round gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The agora was the open public square in an ancient Greek city, used as its marketplace.

clue.text: Dorset's No. 1 referee runs in last place, being more rotund

indicators.note: the number one letter of a word is its first
the letter is taken from where it stood and set down at the very end instead

explanation.surface: A Dorset official runs and finishes last because he is heavier.
explanation.walkthrough: The R of UMPIRE is moved to the end, giving UMPIER after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumpy means short and plump, so dumpier is more rotund; the comparative suits 'being more rotund'.

clue.text: North American hit, a No.1 Dolly composed about a Thanksgiving?

indicators.note: something composed has been put together afresh, so these letters are arranged anew
about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: N for North and A for American
HIT, A, NO and the Roman numeral I for 1, then DOLLY

explanation.surface: An American chart hit, a Dolly Parton number one, written about Thanksgiving.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Dolly Parton; 'No.1' supplies NO and I. The question mark flags Thanksgiving as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thanksgiving is a public day off observed across the whole United States, an example of a nationwide holiday.

clue.text: Band wagon stuck in terrible rain

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so its letters are jumbled
stuck in means lodged inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a van is a goods wagon

explanation.surface: A touring band's wagon gets stuck in a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana was the Seattle grunge group fronted by Kurt Cobain.

clue.text: Ring Madame found in rubbish

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: grot is British slang for rubbish or junk
Mme is the abbreviation of Madame

explanation.surface: A lady's ring turns up in the bin.
explanation.definitionFit: A grommet is a metal or rubber eyelet, a reinforcing ring lining a hole.

clue.text: Old enough to have cigarette in foyer occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept
in means placed inside the other piece

blocks.note: second and fourth letters of foyer
fag is British slang for a cigarette

explanation.surface: A teenager old enough to smoke a cigarette in a theatre lobby now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of age means having reached the legal adult age, so being old enough.

clue.text: Small country hospital injecting famous plumber with last of penicillin

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter only
injecting puts something inside, so one piece takes in the other

blocks.note: san, short for sanatorium, a hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital in a tiny state gives a celebrity plumber a penicillin jab.
explanation.walkthrough: The video-game plumber Mario takes in the N.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny republic enclosed by Italy, one of the smallest sovereign states.

clue.text: 'Mad Dave', Julius, Charlie & Mike pen university guide

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters after it go haywire
to pen is to shut in, so the pair encloses what follows

blocks.note: Julius is the setter, so the setter is ME

explanation.surface: A gang of named characters co-write a guidebook to a university.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves as ME; Julius is this puzzle's setter. C and M enclose U.
explanation.definitionFit: A vade mecum, Latin for 'go with me', is a handbook carried about for constant reference.

clue.text: Caught unknown chap let loose in car-free zone

indicators.note: letting something loose frees it from its order, so its letters scatter

explanation.surface: A mystery man is arrested after being set free in a pedestrian zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let loose' tempts as one phrase, but 'let' joins 'chap' as fodder and only 'loose' signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle path is a route reserved for bicycles, from which motor vehicles are barred.

clue.text: Acrylic rolls short of 50 yards (roughly)

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so some letters are taken away
rolling over turns something round so it reads the other way

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50
Y is the abbreviation for yards

explanation.surface: A shop sells acrylic rolls a little under fifty yards long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolls' looks like a noun for bolts of fabric, but it is the verb telling us to turn the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: Circa, Latin for 'around', is used before dates or figures to mean approximately.

clue.text: Groom might use this Indian food firm memsahib gutted

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the outside letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of memsahib

explanation.surface: A colonial lady is devastated by the food served at her firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' suggests a bridegroom, but here it is someone who tends horses. A memsahib was a European married woman in colonial India.
explanation.definitionFit: A currycomb is a ridged comb a stable hand uses to rub down a horse's coat, a groom's tool.

clue.text: Restored to life, druids seen regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

blocks.note: even letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Ancient druids are spotted walking about once more, as if back from the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Risen describes one who has come back from death, as in the risen Christ.

clue.text: Poet that woman will enjoy on vacation?

indicators.note: a place on vacation is vacated, emptied of its middle, leaving just its ends

blocks.note: first and last letters of enjoy

explanation.surface: A woman looks forward to enjoying herself while away on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy Bysshe Shelley was a leading English Romantic poet.

clue.text: Sat in bus, vulgar Aussie removes electronic bug

indicators.note: removing something takes it away, so a letter goes
sitting in something means being inside it

blocks.note: ocker is slang for a boorish, uncultivated Australian

explanation.surface: A crude Australian on a bus switches off his gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' at the end hints at electronic surveillance, but it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockroach is a common scuttling insect, and bug is a loose word for any insect.

clue.text: Article on Florentine poet is a piece coming along moderately slowly

definitions.text: a piece coming along moderately slowly

blocks.note: Dante Alighieri was born in Florence

explanation.surface: An essay on Dante proceeds slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: An andante is a movement played at a moderate walking pace, from Italian for 'going'.

clue.text: Swear in defence here for trials from Wednesday?

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

blocks.note: to eff is to swear, from the euphemism for the F-word

explanation.surface: A witness swears in their own defence at a trial starting midweek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trials' and 'defence' suggest a courtroom; Sheffield Wednesday is a football club, so its trials are its matches and troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheffield Wednesday FC plays in the city, so it is where Wednesday's trials are endured.

clue.text: Amusing senior detective, an expert from South Africa

explanation.surface: A witty top detective turns out to be a South African specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundi is a South African word, from Nguni, for a learned person or expert.

clue.text: Delay/cancellation for more than half of French railway?

indicators.text: cancellation for more than half of
indicators.note: cancelling over half of a phrase strikes out its larger opening portion

blocks.note: chemin de fer is French for railway

explanation.surface: French rail services are delayed or cancelled across more than half the network.
explanation.walkthrough: Six of the eleven letters, CHEMIN, are struck out, leaving the final word pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To defer is to put off until later, so it means to delay.

clue.text: Call of the highlands found in 17 ode, lyrically

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside the run of letters that follows

blocks.note: the run inside the 17-down answer followed by ode, lyrically

explanation.surface: A highland call appears in a lyrical ode by a Romantic poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 stands for the answer to 17-down, SHELLEY; the word straddles shelleY ODE Lyrically.
explanation.definitionFit: A yodel is the warbling call of Alpine herders, a sound of mountain country.

clue.text: Georgian city — Bath — discovered large pilaster

indicators.note: dis-covered means with the cover taken off, so the outside letters go

blocks.note: an anta is a pilaster at the end of a side wall in classical architecture

explanation.surface: A large Georgian pilaster has been uncovered in Bath, famous for its Georgian buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Georgian' and 'Bath' evoke English 18th-century architecture; Bath is a spa city in England. The city is in the US state of Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlanta is the capital of the American state of Georgia.

clue.text: Father had made a disapproving face

blocks.note: Fr, the title of a priest

explanation.surface: Dad pulled a stern face.
explanation.definitionFit: To frown is to knit the brows in displeasure, so frowned means pulled a disapproving face.

clue.text: Glaring extortion facilitated by The Sun?

definitions.text: Glaring extortion facilitated by The Sun?

blocks.note: surface reading: a blatant overcharge, perhaps by a tabloid newspaper
setter's reading: a theft carried out in the light of the sun rather than at night

explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, so the clue hints at press scandal; read literally, the sun lights up a robbery done in broad day.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a blatant rip-off, robbery so open it might as well be done by sunlight.
